diagnostics.message: module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_cloudtrail.global writes to the audit log bucket (:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log), but nothing orders the trail after the bucket policy. The trail only receives the bucket *name* via module.cloudtrail_baseline:var.s3_bucket_name (sourced from local.audit_log_bucket_id), which carries no dependency on the policy: data.aws_iam_policy_document.audit_log / aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log is a completely separate resource in the root module. CloudTrail validates the destination bucket policy at CreateTrail time and fails with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException when the cloudtrail.amazonaws.com s3:GetBucketAcl / s3:PutObject statements are not yet applied (the provider docs' own example puts depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example] on the trail). Add depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log] to the cloudtrail_baseline module block.

:resource.aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization aggregates from AWS Organizations using aws_iam_role.config_organization, but it only references the role's ARN (aws_iam_role.config_organization[0].arn) and never the resource that grants that role permission to call organizations:DescribeOrganization/ListAccounts, i.e. :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization (AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations). If the aggregator is created first, AWS Config fails with an insufficient-permissions error because the role cannot read the organization. The provider documentation for organization-based aggregation explicitly sets depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.organization] on the aggregator; the same ordering is missing here (a bare depends_on is the only option, since no aggregator attribute can reference the attachment).
